title: The Truth That Broke Me
content:
Siddu wrapped both hands around the warm coffee cup and took another slow sip.

For a few moments, he remained silent, his eyes fixed on the rising steam as though the memories hidden within it were slowly coming back to life.

Sneha didn't interrupt him.

She simply watched him quietly, knowing that the story he was about to tell wasn't an easy one to relive.

After taking a deep breath, Siddu finally looked up.

"After our first year of Intermediate," he began softly, "Shreya suddenly disappeared from my life. It wasn't just that she stopped talking to me... it was as if she had completely vanished."

His voice carried a quiet sadness.

"I tried calling her every single day. I sent countless messages, waited outside places where we usually met, and even asked her friends about her."

He paused for a moment.

"But no one had an answer."

Sneha listened without saying a word.

"Days passed," Siddu continued. "I couldn't eat properly. I couldn't concentrate on my studies. I kept wondering what mistake I had made."

"I kept replaying every conversation we had ever shared. I wondered if I had said something wrong... if I had hurt her without realizing it... or if something terrible had happened to her. Every possible question haunted me."

His eyes remained fixed on the coffee in front of him.

"There were nights when I stayed awake until sunrise, hoping my phone would ring."

"I kept telling myself that maybe she had lost her phone... maybe there was some family problem... maybe tomorrow she would finally call."

A faint smile appeared on his face.

"But tomorrow never came."

His smile slowly faded.

"My parents noticed I wasn't the same anymore. My friends tried to cheer me up, but nothing worked."

"I was physically present everywhere..."

"But mentally, I was trapped in memories of someone who had suddenly disappeared."

He lowered his eyes.

"One day, I finally met Kiran."

A faint smile appeared on his face before disappearing just as quickly.

"I told him everything... how broken I felt... how desperately I wanted to know what had happened to Shreya."

"He didn't interrupt me even once."

"He simply listened."

Siddu's fingers tightened around the coffee cup.

"When I finished speaking, he remained silent for a long time."

"I thought he was trying to comfort me."

"But then..."

He slowly looked at Sneha.

"He said something that completely changed everything."

Siddu stopped speaking for a moment, as though repeating those words still hurt.

Then, in a low voice, he continued.

"Siddu... there's something important I need to tell you."

"I looked at him, completely confused."

"Siddu... Shreya is in love with someone else."

Sneha's eyes widened.

Siddu gave a bitter smile.

"For a few seconds, I honestly thought he was joking."

"I even laughed."

"But Kiran didn't."

"His expression never changed."

"That's when fear slowly crept into my heart."

"I asked him again..."

"What are you talking about?"

"But he repeated the same thing."

"She's betraying you, you idiot. That's why I kept telling you to stay away from her."

"I immediately stood up."

"I couldn't accept those words."

"I almost shouted at him."

"Stop it, Kiran! Don't say things like that about her."

"But he didn't get angry."

"He simply looked at me with pity."

Siddu let out a slow breath.

"I didn't know what to believe."

"On one side... there was the Shreya I loved with all my heart."

"On the other... there was Kiran, my closest friend, who had never lied to me."

"My heart refused to believe Kiran."

"My mind refused to doubt him."

"I felt like I was being torn apart from the inside."

"So, I asked him only one question."

Sneha leaned forward unconsciously.

"What did you ask?"

"I asked him..."

"If what you're saying is true... then tell me who it is."

"Kiran didn't answer immediately."

"He lowered his head."

"For a few seconds, neither of us spoke."

"I could see that even he didn't want to hurt me."

"But eventually..."

"He looked straight into my eyes."

Then he spoke.

Siddu's voice dropped to almost a whisper.

"His name is... Karthik."

The name echoed between them.

The cheerful atmosphere inside the café suddenly felt unusually heavy.

Sneha remained completely silent.

She could see the pain hidden behind Siddu's calm expression.

For Siddu, that single name wasn't merely another person's name. It marked the moment when everything he had believed in began to fall apart. The darkest chapter of his life had just begun.
